title: Reading the Room: Scale-ambiguous Semantic Registration of Sparse VSLAM Maps to Floor Plans in Partially Built Environments

problem.summary: Many robotic construction applications, such as progress tracking, require registering a sensor trajectory to a prior 2D floor plan.
statements: Many robotic construction applications, such as progress tracking, require registering a sensor trajectory to a prior 2D floor plan.

Visual capture is attractive for its low cost and availability, but aligning a visual simultaneous localization and mapping (VSLAM) map to a floor plan is difficult; VSLAM recovers geometry only up to an unknown similarity transform, the sparse point cloud is cross-modal to the symbolic floor plan, sites are only partially built during capture, and construction sites are visually repetitive,
Existing methods address at most two of these challenges.

experiments.summary: We evaluate our method on 3 datasets, spanning 33 trajectories across 3 sites, 14 floors, and 2 countries.

limitations.summary: At its core is a novel robust, classbalanced semantic-geometric energy function that scores candidate transforms without requiring correspondences, remains robust to unbuilt structure and outlier landmarks, and weights rare but distinctive classes equally with common ones.
items: At its core is a novel robust, classbalanced semantic-geometric energy function that scores candidate transforms without requiring correspondences, remains robust to unbuilt structure and outlier landmarks, and weights rare but distinctive classes equally with common ones.
Nonetheless, registration remains unreliable on our hardest site, where low coverage and symmetry drive all methods into incorrect minima.
As our oracle analysis reveals a residual error of approximately 1 m as a result of VSLAM drift, future work should explore non-rigid, floor-plan-conditioned trajectory deformation.
